Say what a period comparison shows, and how sure we can be

Source: R/describe_periods.R
describe_periods.Rd

Turns the output of summarise_periods() into plain-language text with two parts: what happened (the headline) and how sure we are (how the gap between the two averages compares with the usual year-to-year variation).

Usage

describe_periods(periods, variable = NULL, threshold = NULL)

Arguments

periods

A data frame returned by summarise_periods().

variable, threshold

Optional overrides for the temperature measure ("tmax" or "tmin") and threshold used in the wording. By default they are read from the settings stored in periods.

Value

A list with elements

enough_data

TRUE if each period has at least 3 reliable years and at least one of them had a hot day (or night).

title

A one-line claim suitable for a chart title.

headline

A sentence giving the two averages and the gap.

how_sure

A sentence comparing the gap with year-to-year noise.

gap

Later average minus earlier average, in days per year.

low, high

Ends of the rough 95% range for gap.

If enough_data is FALSE, title, headline and how_sure explain what to change and the numeric elements are NA.

Details

The "how sure" part uses a rough 95% range for the difference in means, gap +/- 2 * standard error, where the standard error combines the year-to-year spread and the number of years in each period. It treats years as independent and ignores any trend inside a period, so it is a guide to whether the gap stands out from noise, not a formal significance test.

Examples

ex <- annual_exceedances(threshold = 35)
periods <- summarise_periods(ex, split_year = 2000)
describe_periods(periods)$headline
#> [1] "In 2001–2021 the airport averaged 11.8 days a year with a daily maximum above 35 °C, against 8.2 in 1971–2000. That is 3.6 more hot days a year."
describe_periods(periods)$how_sure
#> [1] "The gap stands out from year-to-year noise: a rough 95% range for the difference is +0.8 to +6.3 days a year. This treats years as independent, so use it as a guide, not a formal test."
